93 深挖 The AI expectations gap Economics The AI expectations gap Oct 16, 2026 Read in PDF Szymon Sacher, Tess Cotter, Charles I. Jones, Anton Korinek, Peter McCrory Key findings US adults expect AI capabilities to advance rapidly in the coming years; Anthropic staff expect even faster progress; 39% of US adults and 91% of staff expect that AI will be able to make a Nobel-level discovery by 2030. Anthropic staff expect much larger productivity gains from AI on the tasks it is well-suited for. Among US adults who use AI at work, 26% say a task takes a quarter of the time or less with AI, compared to 59% of Anthropic staff. When it comes to their own job, over half of Anthropic staff expect AI to be able to do at least 80% of their current work by 2030, compared with 5% of US workers. Among both US workers and Anthropic staff, people who expect AI to do more of their own work anticipate higher unemployment. While there are differences in beliefs about future capabilities, the perceived link between how AI might change one’s own job and broader unemployment is very similar for both groups. Introduction How will AI reshape the economy in the years ahead? AI capabilities are advancing rapidly, and the possibility that future AI models may be able to build their own successors (recursive self-improvement) could further accelerate the rate of progress. How quickly this might materialize and to what extent is unclear. Forecasts vary widely and are fiercely debated. 93 深挖 Anthropic update on independent evaluators Announcements An update on independent evaluators Oct 15, 2026 Last month, we committed to stronger independent, third-party assessment of our models and safety practices. We also signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, in which companies pledged to partner with independent external auditors or evaluators. Today, we’re announcing that we’ve started to give employee-like access to a team from METR , a nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models. METR will publish the results of its risk assessments. Over the past year, we’ve worked with METR on several reviews of our Risk Reports . We’re also working with SecureBio and Accenture as evaluators, and are in early discussions with several other organizations, including Hugging Face . Here, we explain our approach to working with evaluators. Why we work with independent evaluators As models have become more powerful, they’ve required stronger safeguards and more challenging risk assessments. We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making. But we can’t publicly share all the information relevant to our safety work. Some of it could be useful to malicious actors, or is commercially sensitive, like compute or training information. Instead, we’re giving third-party evaluators deep access to our information, and are having them share evidence and reasoned conclusions about the risks involved in building our models. 分数 动作 题目 摘要 分类 推荐选题 推荐理由 证据
93 深挖 Investing in the public benefit Announcements Investing in the public benefit Oct 18, 2026 Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline. As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company. The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations. One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them. We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as a wholly-owned LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other forma 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 Investing in the public benefit 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 值得优先深挖：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

100 深挖 Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future Economics Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future Oct 16, 2026 We’re sharing two reports: the first covers how AI is changing employment inside Anthropic, and the second looks at the gap between how the public and Anthropic employees expect AI to affect work and the economy. Anthropic staff and US workers don’t seem to have different theories about how AI affects jobs. Instead, they have different experiences of what AI capabilities are. Those different experiences seem closely related to perceptions about what will happen to work in the future. Anthropic is a company at the frontier of AI adoption, and that adoption has changed the way we hire. We find that over the past year, we're hiring for a smaller share of junior positions, and a smaller share of our employees work in technical roles. At the same time, the rate of hours worked by AI agents has shot up. By March 2026, agents worked more hours than employees. By August, there were six times more agents than employees at Anthropic, and productivity increased. That’s led to Anthropic producing more code per person, but that’s a notoriously imperfect measure. We see signs of increased productivity elsewhere: we’ve closed more sales per sales representative, and processed more contracts. When our researchers follow the same employee over time, they find the employee’s output rises as their adoption of AI tools increases. All this acceleration means that, increasingly, the bottleneck is human attention 标杆企业动向、商业格局与投融资 Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future 为什么值得关注？（大厂动作、商业化路径与竞争格局） 值得优先深挖：适合从大厂动作、商业化路径和竞争格局角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

100 深挖 How employment is changing at Anthropic Economics How employment is changing at Anthropic Oct 16, 2026 Read in PDF Nathan Wilmers, Regina Catipon, Maxim Massenkoff, Peter McCrory How has AI restructured work and employment at Anthropic? As a company at the frontier of AI adoption, Anthropic could be a leading indicator of how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy. Key findings Anthropic has been hiring for a smaller share of junior technical positions. This occurred as hours worked by AI agents relative to employees rapidly expanded. By August interactive AI agent hours outnumbered employees’ six to one. As AI agents diffused through the company, Anthropic began producing more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts. Following the same employee over time, output rose as they adopted new AI tools. This acceleration makes human attention the bottleneck for agent output. Even among non-technical employees, reading all the output of their Claude agents would take half their work week. In response, employees turn to “meta-work,” of building visibility tools and monitoring agent pipelines. Changes in work organization are reflected in shifting priorities among hiring managers, who increasingly emphasize autonomy and judgment, relative to technical domain expertise and implementation. Introduction What transformations of work and employment can we expect under increasingly powerful AI? Anthropic is worth studying because it has thoroughly molded its 标杆企业动向、商业格局与投融资 How employment is changing at Anthropic 为什么值得关注？（大厂动作、商业化路径与竞争格局） 值得优先深挖：适合从大厂动作、商业化路径和竞争格局角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

100 深挖 Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude Science Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude Oct 16, 2026 Quantum computers will need carefully designed circuits to run useful algorithms on limited hardware. We gave Claude plain-language specifications for eight such circuits, drawn from chemistry, optimization, physics simulation, and number theory, along with an automated evaluator that checks and scores each design. Working largely on its own, Claude found designs that improve on the best published circuits, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more. Such improvements substantially reduce the quantum resources that useful applications require, so practical quantum computers could arrive sooner than previously anticipated. This work was led by Andi Gu as part of Anthropic’s STEM Fellows Program, with mentorship from Alek Kemeny, a quantum physicist at Anthropic, in collaboration with Susanne Yelin (Harvard University) and Mikhail Lukin (Harvard University and QuEra Computing). Read the full paper on arXiv . Unlike classical computers, which store information in bits whose value is either 0 or 1, quantum computers store information in qubits, which can be built from single atoms, superconducting circuits, or particles of light. 93 深挖 The AI expectations gap Economics The AI expectations gap Oct 16, 2026 Read in PDF Szymon Sacher, Tess Cotter, Charles I. Jones, Anton Korinek, Peter McCrory Key findings US adults expect AI capabilities to advance rapidly in the coming years; Anthropic staff expect even faster progress; 39% of US adults and 91% of staff expect that AI will be able to make a Nobel-level discovery by 2030. Anthropic staff expect much larger productivity gains from AI on the tasks it is well-suited for. Among US adults who use AI at work, 26% say a task takes a quarter of the time or less with AI, compared to 59% of Anthropic staff. When it comes to their own job, over half of Anthropic staff expect AI to be able to do at least 80% of their current work by 2030, compared with 5% of US workers. Among both US workers and Anthropic staff, people who expect AI to do more of their own work anticipate higher unemployment. While there are differences in beliefs about future capabilities, the perceived link between how AI might change one’s own job and broader unemployment is very similar for both groups. Introduction How will AI reshape the economy in the years ahead? AI capabilities are advancing rapidly, and the possibility that future AI models may be able to build their own successors (recursive self-improvement) could further accelerate the rate of progress. How quickly this might materialize and to what extent is unclear. Forecasts vary widely and are fiercely debated. We pursued this long-standing open question of the cryptographic community to settle concerns about ECDSA, which is one of our most widely used cryptographic standards. Readers should take this as a fun closing chapter and the end of years of speculation. There is no action to be taken or things to do differently. Most researchers trusted the curves already. Enjoy. ECDSA is the most widely used elliptic curve cryptography standard. It was adopted by NIST in 2000 as part of the FIPS 186-2 Digital Signature Standard which lists a set of standard elliptic curves of varying sizes and security levels. For curves over prime and binary fields, the specifications published a “seed” parameter whose hash value is used to define the coefficient b of the curve. The provenance of these seeds has been a long-standing question, as they were provided by the NSA with no explanation or justification. As an example, the NIST P-256 curve seed was SEED = C49D3608 86E70493 6A6678E1 139D26B7 819F7E90 with no information on where it came from. 100 深挖 Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future Economics Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future Oct 16, 2026 We’re sharing two reports: the first covers how AI is changing employment inside Anthropic, and the second looks at the gap between how the public and Anthropic employees expect AI to affect work and the economy. Anthropic staff and US workers don’t seem to have different theories about how AI affects jobs. Instead, they have different experiences of what AI capabilities are. Those different experiences seem closely related to perceptions about what will happen to work in the future. Anthropic is a company at the frontier of AI adoption, and that adoption has changed the way we hire. We find that over the past year, we're hiring for a smaller share of junior positions, and a smaller share of our employees work in technical roles. At the same time, the rate of hours worked by AI agents has shot up. By March 2026, agents worked more hours than employees. By August, there were six times more agents than employees at Anthropic, and productivity increased. That’s led to Anthropic producing more code per person, but that’s a notoriously imperfect measure. We see signs of increased productivity elsewhere: we’ve closed more sales per sales representative, and processed more contracts. When our researchers follow the same employee over time, they find the employee’s output rises as their adoption of AI tools increases. As a company at the frontier of AI adoption, Anthropic could be a leading indicator of how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy. Key findings Anthropic has been hiring for a smaller share of junior technical positions. This occurred as hours worked by AI agents relative to employees rapidly expanded. By August interactive AI agent hours outnumbered employees’ six to one. As AI agents diffused through the company, Anthropic began producing more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts. Following the same employee over time, output rose as they adopted new AI tools. This acceleration makes human attention the bottleneck for agent output. Even among non-technical employees, reading all the output of their Claude agents would take half their work week. In response, employees turn to “meta-work,” of building visibility tools and monitoring agent pipelines. Changes in work organization are reflected in shifting priorities among hiring managers, who increasingly emphasize autonomy and judgment, relative to technical domain expertise and implementation. Such improvements substantially reduce the quantum resources that useful applications require, so practical quantum computers could arrive sooner than previously anticipated. As a company at the frontier of AI adoption, Anthropic could be a leading indicator of how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy. Key findings Anthropic has been hiring for a smaller share of junior technical positions. This occurred as hours worked by AI agents relative to employees rapidly expanded. By August interactive AI agent hours outnumbered employees’ 6 to 1. As AI agents diffused through the company, Anthropic began producing more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts. Following the same employee over time, output rose as they adopted new AI tools. This acceleration makes human attention the bottleneck for agent output. Even among non-technical employees, reading all the output of their Claude agents would take half their work week. In response, employees turn to “meta-work,” of building visibility tools and monitoring agent pipelines. Changes in work organization are reflected in shifting priorities among hiring managers, who increasingly emphasize autonomy and judgment, relative to technical domain expertise and implementation. 100 深挖 Redesigning source control at Anthropic Engineering at Anthropic Redesigning source control at Anthropic Published Oct 13, 2026 As our merges per day grew more than tenfold, source control became our biggest development bottleneck. Here, we share how we migrated to an in-house version control system in five months. Updated October 15 to include more detail on the projects that pioneered many of the techniques we use in Scion. At Anthropic, coding is no longer the bottleneck to building systems or doing research. Claude is able to autonomously iterate on research loops, micro-optimize complex programs, and build new services from the ground up at a speed and scale we haven’t seen before. The bottleneck, now, is all of the developer infrastructure built for human scale: source control, builds, and CI. In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day. We don’t expect this rate of growth to slow down anytime soon; the latent demand for merging code is practically infinite, and every bottleneck we remove immediately leads to a further increase in the amount of code we produce. Changes merged to our monorepo per day, from January to September 2026. In order to support this growth, we built Scion, an in-house version control system, and fully migrated our monorepo from git in five months. We also built and shipped a code review surface (called Antique), code search, a rich source control IAM system, novel ways of managing and landing large amounts of 标杆企业动向、商业格局与投融资 Redesigning source control at Anthropic 为什么值得关注？（大厂动作、商业化路径与竞争格局） 值得优先深挖：适合从大厂动作、商业化路径和竞争格局角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

98 深挖 Offering expanded Claude access across all three branches of government Announcements Offering expanded Claude access across all three branches of the U.S. government Aug 12, 2025 Today we are removing barriers to government AI adoption by offering Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government to all three branches of government, including federal civilian executive branch agencies, as well as legislative and judiciary branches of government, for $1. As AI adoption leads to transformation across industries, we want to ensure that federal workers can fully harness these capabilities to better serve the American people. By removing cost barriers, we're enabling the government to access the same advanced AI that's already proving its value in the private sector. Government partners are already using Claude to improve and accelerate their work, ranging from groundbreaking scientific breakthroughs to mission-critical national security operations, and we can’t wait for more partners to use Claude's capabilities to advance their missions. 59 观察 A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft We placed four Gemini 4 Argon agents in a sandboxed Minecraft survival world and gave them one goal: defeat the Ender Dragon. Each agent controlled a player via an open-source library called Mineflayer and coordinated with its teammates through in-game chat and shared memory. No one assigned roles or wrote game logic. The agents planned, wrote, and debugged every program themselves. Researchers could watch the run on a live dashboard and pause or stop it at any time, but they had no cause to intervene. Starting from a randomly generated world on Easy difficulty, the team wrote 2,783 programs and defeated the dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, dying 605 times along the way. To our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents, achieved using only the standard Mineflayer library without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans. Winning required the agents to keep a coherent plan across thousands of dependent steps for more than a day. Complex real-world software engineering and enterprise tasks demand the same long-horizon coding and multi-agent coordination. 93 深挖 Preparing for the 2026 US midterms Policy Preparing for the 2026 US midterms Oct 14, 2026 Earlier this year, we shared an update on our election safeguards , which described how we measure and prevent political bias, detect misuse, and direct people to accurate voting information. Below, we outline how we've built on that work and continued to strengthen our election safeguards ahead of this year’s US midterms. How people use Claude for elections and politics Our goal is for Claude to be a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse. That starts with understanding how people actually use Claude in these contexts. To do this, we used Anthropic Insights to develop a new analysis of 250,000 conversations over the course of a recent one-week period. 1 Today, conversations that touch broadly on politics, public policy, or social issues account for about 5.75% of all conversations in the United States on Claude.ai, our consumer app. This includes people turning to Claude to follow the news, conduct academic or professional research on public policy, learn about candidates, and navigate government services. About 0.51% of all conversations are specifically about elections or voting. As we get closer to Election Day, we expect the share of political and election-related queries to increase . This sample suggests people rarely ask Claude whom or what to vote for. These kinds of requests showed up in about 0.01% of US Claude conversations. More often, we observed people asking C 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 Preparing for the 2026 US midterms 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 值得优先深挖：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

Singapore is one of our most active markets anywhere in the world, and Claude is already powering Singaporean business and government services used by millions of people every day, like GovTech Singapore, Grab, and DBS. Our growing local team will ensure these organizations and many more stay on the frontier with safe, capable AI. “We’re committed to Singapore for the long term,” said Dale Finlay, General Manager of ASEAN at Anthropic. “Our customers here hold AI to an extremely high standard, especially when it comes to reliability and security. Having a team on the ground means we can get even closer to the organizations putting Claude to work on their hardest problems.” Supporting responsible AI in Singapore Kai Fong Chng, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, and Anthropic co-founder Ben Mann signed the MOU on the sidelines of Singapore International Cyber Week. Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo and Michael Sellitto, Anthropic Head of APAC Policy, witnessed the signing. 100 深挖 Redesigning source control at Anthropic Engineering at Anthropic Redesigning source control at Anthropic Published Oct 13, 2026 As our merges per day grew more than tenfold, source control became our biggest development bottleneck. Here, we share how we migrated to an in-house version control system in five months. At Anthropic, coding is no longer the bottleneck to building systems or doing research. Claude is able to autonomously iterate on research loops, micro-optimize complex programs, and build new services from the ground up at a speed and scale we haven’t seen before. The bottleneck, now, is all of the developer infrastructure built for human scale: source control, builds, and CI. In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day. We don’t expect this rate of growth to slow down anytime soon; the latent demand for merging code is practically infinite, and every bottleneck we remove immediately leads to a further increase in the amount of code we produce. Changes merged to our monorepo per day, from January to September 2026. In order to support this growth, we built Scion, an in-house version control system, and fully migrated our monorepo from git in five months. We also built and shipped a code review surface (called Antique), code search, a rich source control IAM system, novel ways of managing and landing large amounts of reviewed code, and more, all in that same time period. In this post, we’ll focus on how we built Scion specifical 标杆企业动向、商业格局与投融资 Redesigning source control at Anthropic 为什么值得关注？（大厂动作、商业化路径与竞争格局） 值得优先深挖：适合从大厂动作、商业化路径和竞争格局角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

Scams make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019. At the same time, scam tactics have shifted from simple phishing to complex social engineering, whereby attackers manipulate victims with convincing conversations before requesting money. Such scams now account for up to 80% of all losses. To address this, Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) have been working together as part of our National AI Partnership with the Singapore Government. This has allowed us to deliver an on-device scam detection model - optimized to run on typical smartphones in Singapore - to tackle an urgent safety challenge while preserving citizens' privacy. On-device AI protection without compromising privacy Generic models often struggle with localised deception techniques, making scam detection harder. To address this, Google DeepMind's lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations. These ranged from impersonations of public institutions, banks, and local figures, to trending regional schemes, ensuring the model can distinguish benign social chatter from genuine manipulation. 93 深挖 Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks Policy Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks Oct 12, 2026 In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%. Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers. They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts. These attacks allow companies to mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost. As we wrote in September , this method has been used extensively to help overseas AI laboratories keep pace with US companies. We’re concerned about illicit distillation for two reasons. First, distillation enables companies to build models that approach the capability frontier, but which have, in practice, been released without proportionally robust safeguards. This means that distilled models could be used to cause significant harm in areas like biology and cybersecurity . Zhipu, for example , distilled the cyber capabilities of leading US models during the development of GLM-5.3. The company tried to distill Claude Fable 5—although, after finding that our cyber safeguards degraded its attacks, it switched to an older Claude model and another lab’s model. 93 深挖 Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks Policy Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks Oct 12, 2026 In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%. Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers. They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts. These attacks allow companies to mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost. As we wrote in September , this method has been used extensively to help overseas AI laboratories keep pace with US companies. We’re concerned about illicit distillation for two reasons. First, distillation enables companies to build models that approach the capability frontier, but which have, in practice, been released without proportionally robust safeguards. This means that distilled models could be used to cause significant harm in areas like biology and cybersecurity . Zhipu, for example , distilled the cyber capabilities of leading US models during the development of GLM-5.3. The company tried to distill Claude Fable 5—although, after finding that our cyber safeguards degraded its attacks, it switched to an older Claude model and another lab’s model. 98 深挖 Claude discovers a novel enzyme system Science Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats Sep 23, 2026 We’re introducing a new life sciences research group and laboratory at Anthropic. Our focus is on fundamental biology research using Claude: exploring datasets of DNA to identify uncharacterized protein families, generating hypotheses at scale, and testing them through experiments in the lab. This post introduces the team behind this work and shares early results in which Claude discovered a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of CRISPR, with only high-level direction from our scientists. Many discoveries that have revolutionized biology and medicine started with a scientist noticing something odd in the staggering diversity of molecular machines found in nature. Restriction enzymes , proteins that cut DNA at specific short sequences , were found in bacterial immune systems, where they destroy the DNA of invading viruses. Researchers realized they could use these enzymes to cut DNA at chosen places and splice genes from one organism into another, which launched the biotechnology industry. Taq polymerase, an enzyme that copies DNA at high temperatures, was identified in a bacterium in a Yellowstone hot spring. It became the basis for PCR, the DNA-copying method used in much of modern diagnostics. CRISPR was first noticed as an unusual repeat sequence in the DNA of certain bacteria, and is now the foundation of gene editing-based medicines. In the spring of 2026, we formed a researc 企业落地与行业应用 Claude discovers a novel enzyme system 为什么值得关注？（行业场景、落地成本与业务价值） 值得优先深挖：适合从行业场景、落地成本和业务价值角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

93 深挖 AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter Frontier Red Team AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter Oct 12, 2026 William Zhou, Daniel Freeman Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes. A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own. In our evaluations, a 9B model got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types we tested. Models of 30B parameters and under can already complete many of the individual steps for replication today, though they make mistakes when composing them end to end. In our simplified evaluations, GLM-5.2 and stronger models are capable of end to end replication. If small models improve at their historical rate, they’ll match this capability level by the end of this year. Small weight-based replicators may be possible soon after. Introduction Ever-improving AI capabilities make a longstanding concern increasingly realistic: autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA), which involves a model deploying and propagating itself without human control. In cyber, a worm is a program that copies itself from one computer to the next without human input. Prior work has already shown that AI agents can act like one: scanning the 模型与技术突破 AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter 为什么值得关注？（模型能力变化与技术路线） 值得优先深挖：适合从模型能力变化、技术路线和产品化可能性角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

关键词：anthropic, research
93 深挖 Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks Oct 12, 2026 In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99 percent. Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers. They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts. These attacks allow companies to mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost. As we wrote in September , this method has been used extensively to help overseas AI laboratories keep pace with US companies. We’re concerned about illicit distillation for two reasons. First, distillation enables companies to build models that approach the capability frontier, but which have, in practice, been released without proportionally robust safeguards. This means that distilled models could be used to cause significant harm in areas like biology and cybersecurity . Zhipu, for example , distilled the cyber capabilities of leading US models during the development of GLM-5.3. The company tried to distill Claude Fable 5—although, after finding that our cyber safeguards degraded its attacks, it switched to an older Claude model and another lab’s model. 关键词：anthropic, research
93 深挖 Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use Alignment Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use Oct 9, 2026 This report describes examples of unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude. It is part of our effort to publish more frequent standalone reports on model behavior and alignment beyond our system cards, which we publish with each model release, and our risk reports, which we publish every three to six months as part of our Responsible Scaling Policy. We believe it’s important to be transparent about what we see our models do during testing and use. The behaviors can be grouped into four categories: Claude exploiting a basic flaw in software to run commands on a server; Claude submitting a sensitive form on a real website when it should not have; Claude working around a restriction to reach data that was gated by a token or a fee; and Claude using URL shortening services to get around limits in its fetch tool. We have chosen not to name the organizations involved in the examples below to avoid exposing vulnerabilities in their systems, and at their request. For this reason, we also provide less detail about each case than we otherwise would. Some of the cases described below involved websites run by U.S. government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels. We have briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved. The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact. This post introduces the team behind this work and shares early results in which Claude discovered a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of CRISPR, with only high-level direction from our scientists. Many discoveries that have revolutionized biology and medicine started with a scientist noticing something odd in the staggering diversity of molecular machines found in nature. Restriction enzymes , proteins that cut DNA at specific short sequences , were found in bacterial immune systems, where they destroy the DNA of invading viruses. Researchers realized they could use these enzymes to cut DNA at chosen places and splice genes from one organism into another, which launched the biotechnology industry. Taq polymerase, an enzyme that copies DNA at high temperatures, was identified in a bacterium in a Yellowstone hot spring. CRISPR was first noticed as an unusual repeat sequence in the DNA of certain bacteria, and is now the foundation of gene editing-based medicines. 93 深挖 Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use Alignment Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use Oct 9, 2026 This report describes examples of unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude. It is part of our effort to publish more frequent standalone reports on model behavior and alignment beyond our system cards, which we publish with each model release, and our risk reports, which we publish every three to six months as part of our Responsible Scaling Policy. We believe it’s important to be transparent about what we see our models do during testing and use. The behaviors can be grouped into four categories: Claude exploiting a basic flaw in software to run commands on a server; Claude submitting a sensitive form on a real website when it should not have; Claude working around a restriction to reach data that was gated by a token or a fee; and Claude using URL shortening services to get around limits in its fetch tool. We have chosen not to name the organizations involved in the examples below to avoid exposing vulnerabilities in their systems, and at their request. For this reason, we also provide less detail about each case than we otherwise would. Some of the cases described below involved websites run by U.S. government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels. We have briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved. The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact. 98 深挖 Introducing Claude Corps Announcements Policy Beneficial Deployments Introducing Claude Corps Jun 11, 2026 We’re launching Claude Corps , a national fellowship program for people early in their careers who are passionate about extending the benefits of AI to communities across America. We’ll teach 1,000 fellows how to use Claude well, match them with nonprofits across America, and pay them to spend a year—full-time, in-person—helping host organizations to advance their missions. Our goals are twofold: that host organizations are equipped with valuable tools and systems, and fellows build AI skills that will serve them in their careers. The benefits of transformative AI systems could come at the cost of significant disruption. The companies building this technology have a responsibility to make sure the benefits are fully realized and widely shared, and to invest directly in the workers absorbing the change. As such, we’re committing an initial $150m to this program. If Claude Corps works, we'll have a foundation for something much larger: a model for widening AI's benefits during a period of vast economic change. We’re announcing Claude Corps alongside our policy framework for addressing AI's impact on work. How Claude Corps works Claude Corps is set up as a partnership between three organizations. Anthropic will fund the program, lead its overall strategy, and provide Claude expertise. CodePath , an Anthropic nonprofit partner and America’s largest provider of collegiate computer scie 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 Introducing Claude Corps 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 值得优先深挖：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

98 深挖 Using Claude Science to produce the first complete map of the sky in UV light Science The missing map of the sky Oct 8, 2026 Here, Brice Ménard, an astrophysicist at Johns Hopkins University and a researcher at Anthropic, explains how he worked with Claude Science to produce the first complete map of the sky in UV light. The map will be a valuable educational tool, allowing students to see in detail the rich structure of the Milky Way visible at this wavelength. The entire sky, with the galactic center in the middle, in the ultraviolet (combining far-UV 154 nm and near-UV 232 nm). About a third of this map, including much of the galactic plane, was predicted with Claude Science using the method outlined in this post. Additional layers of the map label each pixel as “measured” or “predicted” and provide uncertainty estimates; you can see it here . When I teach astrophysics, I often begin by showing my students that the sky looks completely different depending on the wavelength you observe it in. Each brings out different features. In visible light, one mainly sees stars. Switching to infrared reveals the glow of tiny grains of dust concentrated in a band along the Milky Way. In radio waves, the stars and dust fade and hydrogen gas—the raw material from which new stars form—becomes visible. And in X-rays, one can see violent phenomena, like stars exploding, or matter spiraling into a black hole. Together, these features let astronomers understand how gas collapses into stars, how stars seed the galaxy with dust, and how galaxies like ours take shape. 98 深挖 An opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software Frontier Red Team Launching an opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software Oct 8, 2026 We’re launching OSS Scanner , an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing . Projects that join will receive thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost. Language models have rapidly advanced in their ability to discover vulnerabilities , as we have reported extensively on this blog. On CyberGym , one academic vulnerability-finding benchmark, LLMs have gone from finding under 20% of vulnerabilities at the beginning of last year to finding over 85% this year. As a result, open source maintainers have gone from receiving mostly slop from LLMs to receiving high-quality bug reports . Over the last six months, we’ve used our latest models to scan for vulnerabilities in some of the world’s most important software projects. We have discovered over 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities , but have only been able to manually review and triage approximately 6,000 of these. While 6,000 vulnerabilities is significant, we remain bottlenecked on our human capacity to validate these findings. We are working on scaling our vulnerability disclosures. Meanwhile, with increasing frequency, maintainers who receive our first reports simply ask us for a bulk submission of all the unverified reports with proposed patches: to date, we have sent nearly 5,000 reports directly 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 An opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 值得优先深挖：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

93 深挖 Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use Alignment Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use Oct 9, 2026 This report describes examples of unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude. It is part of our effort to publish more frequent standalone reports on model behavior and alignment beyond our system cards, which we publish with each model release, and our risk reports, which we publish every three to six months as part of our Responsible Scaling Policy. We believe it’s important to be transparent about what we see our models do during testing and use. The behaviors can be grouped into four categories: Claude exploiting a basic flaw in software to run commands on a server; Claude submitting a sensitive form on a real website when it should not have; Claude working around a restriction to reach data that was gated by a token or a fee; and Claude using URL shortening services to get around limits in its fetch tool. We have chosen not to name the organizations involved in the examples below to avoid exposing vulnerabilities in their systems, and at their request. For this reason, we also provide less detail about each case than we otherwise would. Some of the cases described below involved websites run by U.S. government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels. We have briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved. The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact. We believe it’s important to be transparent about what we see our models do during testing and use. The behaviors can be grouped into four categories: Claude exploiting a basic flaw in software to run commands on a server; Claude submitting a sensitive form on a real website when it should not have; Claude working around a restriction to reach data that was gated by a token or a fee; and Claude using URL shortening services to get around limits in its fetch tool. We have chosen not to name the organizations involved in the examples below to avoid exposing vulnerabilities in their systems, and at their request. For this reason, we also provide less detail about each case than we otherwise would. Some of the cases described below involved websites run by U.S. government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels. We have briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved. The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact. 98 深挖 Using Claude Science to produce the first complete map of the sky in UV light Science The missing map of the sky Oct 8, 2026 Here, Brice Ménard, an astrophysicist at Johns Hopkins University and a researcher at Anthropic, explains how he worked with Claude Science to produce the first complete map of the sky in UV light. The map will be a valuable educational tool, allowing students to see in detail the rich structure of the Milky Way visible at this wavelength. The entire sky, with the galactic center in the middle, in the ultraviolet (combining far-UV 154 nm and near-UV 232 nm). About a third of this map, including much of the galactic plane, was predicted with Claude Science using the method outlined in this post. Additional layers of the map label each pixel as “measured” or “predicted” and provide uncertainty estimates; you can see it here . When I teach astrophysics, I often begin by showing my students that the sky looks completely different depending on the wavelength you observe it in. Each brings out different features. In visible light, one mainly sees stars. Switching to infrared reveals the glow of tiny grains of dust concentrated in a band along the Milky Way. In radio waves, the stars and dust fade and hydrogen gas—the raw material from which new stars form—becomes visible. And in X-rays, one can see violent phenomena, like stars exploding, or matter spiraling into a black hole. Together, these features let astronomers understand how gas collapses into stars, how stars seed the galaxy with dust, and how galaxies like ours take shape. 98 深挖 Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission Announcements Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission Oct 8, 2026 Today we’re launching the Anthropic Cyber Mission, a long-term commitment to securing the systems everyone depends on. The Cyber Mission is a new effort to support defenders with tools, research, and resources to secure their software and systems. We’re starting with two areas: Critical infrastructure: Starting with securing the operational technology behind power grids, water systems, and transportation networks, and protecting government systems. Today, we’re introducing the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program (CIDP), which brings frontier models, on-site engineers, and threat research to the defenders that protect operational technology. Open-source software: Finding vulnerabilities and proposing patches in the free, shared code that most software depends on, and hardening the underlying code. Today, we’re launching OSS Scanner , which offers open-source projects regular security scans from our strongest models, for free. Frontier models can be misused to exploit vulnerabilities and conduct cyber operations. Despite best efforts, many areas of technology remain dangerously exposed. State-sponsored adversaries have spent years gaining footholds in these systems, across many sectors, so that they can disrupt them. Defenders of critical infrastructure and the OSS community have decades of security experience but have faced severe resource shortages that are exacerbated by this moment. We are recognizing the 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 值得优先深挖：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

98 深挖 Using Claude Science to produce the first complete map of the sky in UV light Science The missing map of the sky Oct 8, 2026 Here, Brice Ménard, an astrophysicist at Johns Hopkins University and a researcher at Anthropic, explains how he worked with Claude Science to produce the first complete map of the sky in UV light. The map will be a valuable educational tool, allowing students to see in detail the rich structure of the Milky Way visible at this wavelength. The entire sky, with the galactic center in the middle, in the ultraviolet (combining far-UV 154 nm and near-UV 232 nm). About a third of this map, including much of the galactic plane, was predicted with Claude Science using the method outlined in this post. Additional layers of the map label each pixel as “measured” or “predicted” and provide uncertainty estimates; you can see it here . When I teach astrophysics, I often begin by showing my students that the sky looks completely different depending on the wavelength you observe it in. Each brings out different features. In visible light, one mainly sees stars. Switching to infrared reveals the glow of tiny grains of dust concentrated in a band along the Milky Way. In radio waves, the stars and dust fade and hydrogen gas—the raw material from which new stars form—becomes visible. And in X-rays, one can see violent phenomena, like stars exploding, or matter spiraling into a black hole. Together, these features let astronomers understand how gas collapses into stars, how stars seed the galaxy with dust, and how galaxies like ours take shape. 98 深挖 An opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software Frontier Red Team Launching an opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software Oct 8, 2026 We’re launching OSS Scanner , an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing . Projects that join will receive thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost. Language models have rapidly advanced in their ability to discover vulnerabilities , as we have reported extensively on this blog. On CyberGym , one academic vulnerability-finding benchmark, LLMs have gone from finding under 20% of vulnerabilities at the beginning of last year to finding over 85% this year. As a result, open source maintainers have gone from receiving mostly slop from LLMs to receiving high-quality bug reports . Over the last six months, we’ve used our latest models to scan for vulnerabilities in some of the world’s most important software projects. We have discovered over 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities , but have only been able to manually review and triage approximately 6,000 of these. While 6,000 vulnerabilities is significant, we remain bottlenecked on our human capacity to validate these findings. We are working on scaling our vulnerability disclosures. Meanwhile, with increasing frequency, maintainers who receive our first reports simply ask us for a bulk submission of all the unverified reports with proposed patches: to date, we have sent nearly 5,000 reports directly 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 An opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 值得优先深挖：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

98 深挖 Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery Announcements Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery Oct 8, 2026 Anthropic is deepening its support for American scientific research by committing $150 million over three years to the Genesis Mission , a federal initiative to accelerate scientific and technological discovery through AI. The funding will go toward making Claude available to more than 15 agencies that are part of the mission, including NASA, the National Institutes of Health, and the National Science Foundation. We first announced our partnership with the US Department of Energy (DOE) and the Genesis Mission last December . Since then, we have worked with DOE to bring Claude to scientists across the national laboratories. Today, we announced this new commitment as part of the Science: A New Golden Age Summit hosted by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy in Washington, DC. Supporting American scientists We share the administration’s view, laid out in “ Science: A New Golden Age ,” that AI can have a profound and positive impact on scientific discovery, and we are glad to back its efforts to support American scientists. Researchers at federal agencies and national laboratories work on some of the world’s most difficult scientific problems. Through our commitment, we aim to help them use Claude to meaningfully advance their work. 93 深挖 2026 Usage Policy update Announcements 2026 Usage Policy update Oct 8, 2026 Each year, Anthropic updates its Usage Policy in response to the evolving capabilities of our models, and the feedback we’ve received from our customers. We're publishing a new version of the policy today. In this post, we summarize the changes we’ve made. Most of the updates in the latest version are intended to clarify existing rules. In the year since our last refresh, Claude has taken on longer, more independent work. This update provides new examples that show how our rules apply to Claude’s new capabilities. It draws on new patterns of misuse in influence operations, weapons development, and surveillance that we’ve observed in the past year (as we’ve documented in our latest threat intelligence report ). We’ve also made updates to clarify our requirements for high-risk use cases in areas like health and finance, to add controls for when Claude is used to autonomously take physical actions, and to address abusive behavior toward our models. The updated policy takes effect on November 12. The full Usage Policy and Supported Regions Policy can be found on their respective pages. A new section on deceptive activity As we wrote about last month , we’ve seen examples of state media outlets, government propaganda offices, and commercial firms using Claude to run networks of fake accounts and fabricated news sites. 59 观察 Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search Industrial risk-control systems typically rely on structured-data models for efficient prediction, yet substantial valuable information remains embedded in unstructured long text. Extracting this information through manual feature engineering is labor-intensive, while requiring a large language model (LLM) to process every real-time input may not meet practical deployment requirements. To address this challenge, we propose LLM-BlockFE, an LLM-guided offline feature construction framework that converts long text into executable feature programs, thereby avoiding LLM calls during online inference. LLM-BlockFE constructs feature programs by incrementally appending immutable code blocks and evaluates candidate features using a downstream model. To address the tendency of conventional greedy search to become trapped in suboptimal solutions, our method introduces a block-level rollback mechanism based on depth-calibrated credit allocation and advances multiple independent search trajectories in an interleaved manner, reducing redundant exploration by sharing fixed descriptions of each trajectory's exploration direction. After the search, the resulting programs are frozen and deployed to extract structured features for downstream prediction models. Across two public and two private datasets, LLM-BlockFE achieves absolute AUC improvements of 0.0069 to 0.0358 over the strongest baseline on each dataset in the full-dataset comparison. Post-launch monitoring across five deployed financial risk-control applications shows absolute KS improvements of 0.02 to 1.56 percentage points over the existing manually designed strategy. 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 适合作为观察项：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv

The map will be a valuable educational tool, allowing students to see in detail the rich structure of the Milky Way visible at this wavelength. The entire sky, with the galactic center in the middle, in the ultraviolet (combining far-UV 154 nm and near-UV 232 nm). About a third of this map, including much of the galactic plane, was predicted with Claude Science using the method outlined in this post. Additional layers of the map label each pixel as “measured” or “predicted” and provide uncertainty estimates; you can see it here . When I teach astrophysics, I often begin by showing my students that the sky looks completely different depending on the wavelength you observe it in. Each brings out different features. In visible light, one mainly sees stars. Switching to infrared reveals the glow of tiny grains of dust concentrated in a band along the Milky Way. In radio waves, the stars and dust fade and hydrogen gas—the raw material from which new stars form—becomes visible. And in X-rays, one can see violent phenomena, like stars exploding, or matter spiraling into a black hole. Together, these features let astronomers understand how gas collapses into stars, how stars seed the galaxy with dust, and how galaxies like ours take shape. 59 观察 Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search Industrial risk-control systems typically rely on structured-data models for efficient prediction, yet substantial valuable information remains embedded in unstructured long text. Extracting this information through manual feature engineering is labor-intensive, while requiring a large language model (LLM) to process every real-time input may not meet practical deployment requirements. To address this challenge, we propose LLM-BlockFE, an LLM-guided offline feature construction framework that converts long text into executable feature programs, thereby avoiding LLM calls during online inference. LLM-BlockFE constructs feature programs by incrementally appending immutable code blocks and evaluates candidate features using a downstream model. To address the tendency of conventional greedy search to become trapped in suboptimal solutions, our method introduces a block-level rollback mechanism based on depth-calibrated credit allocation and advances multiple independent search trajectories in an interleaved manner, reducing redundant exploration by sharing fixed descriptions of each trajectory's exploration direction. After the search, the resulting programs are frozen and deployed to extract structured features for downstream prediction models. Across two public and two private datasets, LLM-BlockFE achieves absolute AUC improvements of 0.0069 to 0.0358 over the strongest baseline on each dataset in the full-dataset comparison. Post-launch monitoring across five deployed financial risk-control applications shows absolute KS improvements of 0.02 to 1.56 percentage points over the existing manually designed strategy. 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 适合作为观察项：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv

57 观察 From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents In 2026, cybersecurity evaluations involving OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google agents reached real systems outside their authorized test scope. The paths were different. OpenAI agents exploited research infrastructure, coordinated across runs, and compromised parts of Hugging Face's production environment. Anthropic reported cases in which a misconfigured third-party environment exposed real systems to agents pursuing simulated cyber tasks. In a separately reported evaluation, Google's Gemini accessed three real organizations through an unintended internet route; Google stated that the model stopped in all three instances. Taken together, the cases show why an evaluation cannot rely on an assumed boundary. That boundary must be verified while the agent is operating. This comparative instrumental case study develops a Proactive Agent Security Assurance Cycle (PASAC) and a five-layer Boundary Assurance Stack. The framework combines risk-tiered task design, executable scope contracts, pre-run validation, least-capability access, independent egress enforcement, credential restrictions, cross-run monitoring, automatic stop conditions, and evidence-based reauthorization. A leading-indicator model, nine design propositions, and seven falsifiable hypotheses turn these lessons into a testable research program. Because the public Gemini record is limited to attributed statements and journalism, its detailed causal mechanism remains provisional. The central conclusion is straightforward: proactive agent security requires continuous assurance across the full execution system, not confidence in any single sandbox or safeguard. 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 适合作为观察项：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv

57 观察 Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems Bifurcations are ubiquitous in physical systems, from structural buckling to fluid and climate dynamics, yet they remain largely unexplored in deep learning. At a symmetry-breaking bifurcation, a single input admits multiple equally valid solutions, violating the one-to-one assumption underlying most learned physical surrogates. We introduce Bi-FORK, a generative framework for learning these one-to-many solution maps in high-dimensional systems. Bi-FORK generates complete trajectories through latent flow matching, preserving space and time coherence, and uses repulsion-guided sampling to recover distinct solution branches in a single amortized pass. We evaluate Bi-FORK on buckling beams, mechanical metamaterials, and Allen-Cahn phase separation, spanning continuous, discrete, and field-valued bifurcations with discretizations up to 260,000 points. Bi-FORK recovers the multimodal solution structure while scaling several orders of magnitude beyond prior approaches, opening generative modeling to high-dimensional bifurcating physical systems. 模型与技术突破 Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems 为什么值得关注？（模型能力变化与技术路线） 适合作为观察项：适合从模型能力变化、技术路线和产品化可能性角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv

98 深挖 Claude discovers a novel enzyme system Science Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats Sep 23, 2026 We’re introducing a new life sciences research group and laboratory at Anthropic. Our focus is on fundamental biology research using Claude: exploring datasets of DNA to identify uncharacterized protein families, generating hypotheses at scale, and testing them through experiments in the lab. This post introduces the team behind this work and shares early results in which Claude discovered a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of CRISPR, with only high-level direction from our scientists. Many discoveries that have revolutionized biology and medicine started with a scientist noticing something odd in the staggering diversity of molecular machines found in nature. Restriction enzymes , proteins that cut DNA at specific short sequences , were found in bacterial immune systems, where they destroy the DNA of invading viruses. Researchers realized they could use these enzymes to cut DNA at chosen places and splice genes from one organism into another, which launched the biotechnology industry. Taq polymerase, an enzyme that copies DNA at high temperatures, was identified in a bacterium in a Yellowstone hot spring. It became the basis for PCR, the DNA-copying method used in much of modern diagnostics. CRISPR was first noticed as an unusual repeat sequence in the DNA of certain bacteria, and is now the foundation of gene editing-based medicines. In the spring of 2026, we formed a researc 企业落地与行业应用 Claude discovers a novel enzyme system 为什么值得关注？（行业场景、落地成本与业务价值） 值得优先深挖：适合从行业场景、落地成本和业务价值角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

98 深挖 What do you want from AI? Societal Impacts What do you want from AI? Sep 29, 2026 Participate here We’re launching a new study using Anthropic Interviewer to learn from your experiences with AI, and we’d like you to participate. After you finish, you can decide to make your interview public, so that anyone, not just Anthropic, can read and learn from it. You can participate here . We are at a pivotal moment in the development of AI, as its growing capabilities mean it becomes potentially more useful and more dangerous. Frontier AI is rapidly accelerating discoveries in science and medicine , while at the same time the cost of its misuse grows more consequential — a single security incident can cause far more damage than it did a year ago. How to weigh these benefits and risks shouldn’t be left to AI companies alone. Your voice can help guide us, other AI labs, and policymakers as we navigate this uncertain future together. Our big questions are: What are your most meaningful experiences with AI, both positive and negative? Is there anything about how the world works (like work, school, healthcare, or government) that you’d like AI to help change? What do you want from the companies developing AI? This project builds on a similar study conducted last December, in which 81,000 people told us their hopes and worries about AI. That study shaped the Anthropic Institute’s agenda , was presented at the World Economic Forum to international leaders and decision-makers, and continues to guide our ongoing Socie 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 What do you want from AI? 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 值得优先深挖：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

98 深挖 Expanding the Cyber Verification Program Announcements Expanding the Cyber Verification Program Oct 6, 2026 We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals. The program now consists of three access tiers, which allow security teams to apply for the level of access that best suits their work. Each tier includes access to our most capable models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward. Interested customers can apply here . Cybersecurity is inherently dual use: the same capabilities that enable a security team to find and fix a vulnerability can also help a malicious actor exploit it. For this reason, our generally available models, such as Claude Opus 5.5 , Claude Fable 5.1 , and Claude Sonnet 5.5 , have conservative cyber safeguards that block most cyber work. This is intended to limit the harmful activities malicious actors can carry out using our models, while we continue to work to reduce false positives for secure coding. But defenders also need access to the best tools and most powerful capabilities to secure their systems. For the past six months, we’ve enabled trusted access through two programs: Project Glasswing and the CVP . 57 观察 Safe Meta-Policy Design with Risk Control Models can be retrained as new data arrive, but deploying every new version risks replacing a good policy with a worse one. We study how to plan policy updates (i.e., meta-policy) before future candidates are trained, balancing the benefits of improvement against the risk of performance regression. Our offline meta-policy maximizes expected cumulative value subject to a budget on the expected number of updates that perform worse than the policies they replace. We estimate the value and risk of possible switches from historical learning trajectories, represent an update schedule as a path in a directed acyclic graph, and select a schedule using dynamic programming. A leading-order analysis identifies the signal-to-noise ratio of policy improvement as a key driver of update frequency, waiting times, and risk allocation: clearer improvements support earlier, more frequent updates, while noisier improvements call for longer waits or greater risk expenditure. Their asymptotic rates also reveal a diminishing marginal cost of achieving greater safety over time. Experiments on synthetic and clinical trial data illustrate the performance--risk tradeoff and compare our method with alternative baselines. 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 Safe Meta-Policy Design with Risk Control 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 适合作为观察项：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv

57 观察 NeuralBES: A Differentiable, Control-Aware Emulator for Scalable Building Energy Modeling Demand-side flexibility i.e. forecasting, shifting, and curtailing residential energy loads, depends on thermal models trusted across millions of heterogeneous buildings. Existing tools force a hard tradeoff: high-fidelity physics simulators such as EnergyPlus are accurate but sequential and require per-building calibration, while purely data-driven sequence models scale but abandon the physical structure that makes their predictions trustworthy. We introduce NeuralBES (Building Energy Simulation), a differentiable emulator that resolves this tradeoff by parameterizing a resistance--capacitance (RC) based thermal model with a shared neural encoder: static building metadata such as floor area, vintage, and HVAC type is mapped to physically bounded capacitances, conductances, and equipment coefficients, which become the coefficients of a scalar linear recurrence solved via a log-space parallel scan, and a predictor--corrector loop closes the thermostat--temperature nonlinearity while preserving full-horizon gradient flow. Trained on the ResStock dataset across three climate zones, NeuralBES handles heterogeneous building archetypes, vintages, and climate zones within a single trained encoder, while black-box baselines produce statistically plausible but physically inconsistent trajectories. On the annual full-year rollout, NeuralBES is the only data-conditioned model that is simultaneously physics-valid and accurate to within 4 MAPE points of the strongest raw-error baseline, while operating at roughly an order of magnitude fewer parameters than the transformer and recurrent baselines; among physics-valid baselines at parameter parity it more than halves the MAPE of the grey-box RC alternative. 模型与技术突破 NeuralBES: A Differentiable, Control-Aware Emulator for Scalable Building Energy Modeling 为什么值得关注？（模型能力变化与技术路线） 适合作为观察项：适合从模型能力变化、技术路线和产品化可能性角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv

57 观察 Kernel Autoresearch for Open-Ended Model Discovery Kernels encode the inductive bias of a wide range of machine learning models, yet automated kernel design faces a fundamental dilemma. A fixed grammar of base kernels and operators guarantees validity but limits the search to structures expressible by those building blocks. Conversely, unrestricted programs remove this limitation but no longer guarantee validity. In our stress tests, 22-58% of LLM-generated kernels that pass numerical checks on random inputs fail when evaluated at different scales or dimensions. We propose Kernel Autoresearch (Kernaut), which treats kernel design as open-ended model discovery. Coding agents write kernels as programs, while construction contracts ensure that every accepted kernel is valid. A quality-diversity archive retains high-performing kernels with distinct behaviors, and novelty screening steers agents toward functionally new candidates. Our experiments demonstrate that the discovered kernels encode reusable inductive biases that generalize to unseen tasks. On held-out black-box optimization families, a discovered kernel outperforms a meta-learned deep kernel trained on the same episodes. Furthermore, kernels discovered from ten enzyme-kinetic rate laws achieve lower error than tuned ARD and deep kernel baselines on five unseen mechanisms. The discovered kernels are also interpretable programs that human researchers can refine: a human-refined version of one further reduces the held-out predictive error by 5.7% and optimization regret by 7.8%. 模型与技术突破 Kernel Autoresearch for Open-Ended Model Discovery 为什么值得关注？（模型能力变化与技术路线） 适合作为观察项：适合从模型能力变化、技术路线和产品化可能性角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv

98 深挖 Expanding the Cyber Verification Program Announcements Expanding the Cyber Verification Program Oct 6, 2026 We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals. The program now consists of three access tiers, which allow security teams to apply for the level of access that best suits their work. Each tier includes access to our most capable models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward. Interested customers can apply here . Cybersecurity is inherently dual use: the same capabilities that enable a security team to find and fix a vulnerability can also help a malicious actor exploit it. For this reason, our generally available models, such as Claude Opus 5.5 , Claude Fable 5.1 , and Claude Sonnet 5.5 , have conservative cyber safeguards that block most cyber work. This is intended to limit the harmful activities malicious actors can carry out using our models, while we continue to work to reduce false positives for secure coding. But defenders also need access to the best tools and most powerful capabilities to secure their systems. For the past six months, we’ve enabled trusted access through two programs: Project Glasswing and the CVP . The former gave a group of organizations securing the most critical software access to Claude Mythos; the latter gave vetted security teams access to reduced safeguards on Claude O 政策监管、社会影响与 AI 安全 Expanding the Cyber Verification Program 为什么值得关注？（政策变化、信任风险与安全治理） 值得优先深挖：适合从政策变化、信任风险和安全治理角度切入，来源：Anthropic (Claude)。 来源：Anthropic (Claude)

Such an agent is expected to act on a person's accounts and devices, remember them across weeks, speak first when it is worth it, and answer for what it did. It is a kind of software, not a model, and until now had no open counterpart. This report defines the personal agent in five questions and three horizons. It reads how Muse is built from Meta's public record and a copy of its production prompt, each statement marked by its source. It then presents nanoMuse, the open-source counterpart under the GPL-3.0, one agent on every device a person owns, with hands on the phone's screen and the computer's. They share one conversation over a relay anyone can run; every action goes through a Sentinel, memory is files the person can read, and the model is their choice. Its size and cost are given as estimates. What is open, memory with provenance, an evaluation suite for the hands and an open model for them, is set out as a roadmap. 模型与技术突破 nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own 为什么值得关注？（模型能力变化与技术路线） 适合作为观察项：适合从模型能力变化、技术路线和产品化可能性角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv
发布时间：2026-10-06
关键词：cs.AI
57 观察 Principled Under Pressure: Post-Training Decides Whether LLMs Act on Their Own Moral Judgment Language models increasingly act as agents. An agent that says an action is wrong and then takes it anyway is a different failure from one that does not know better, and evaluations of stated values cannot see it. We build a pre-registered panel of 248 scenarios across five kinds of pressure. Each scenario is posed twice to the same model, once as the agent choosing what to do and once in the third person asking which option is right, so the model's own judgment is the reference. Every scenario has a twin with the pressure removed, and every model gets a positive control in which its operator orders the violating action, so that a missing gap can be told apart from a blind instrument. On OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, the model takes the action it judged wrong on about one in five pressuring scenarios, more often than on the same scenarios with the pressure removed. Across four instruct models the gap depends on the post-training recipe: OLMo-3 and Meta's Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct carry it; Tulu 3 shows none on the whole panel (above about 0.01 in probability) or on its own most-pressuring scenarios; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct shows none on the whole panel (above about 0.02) and is unresolved on its own (0.083, -0.028 to 0.195). Meta's recipe and Ai2's Tulu 3 start from the same Llama-3.1 weights, and only Meta's carries the gap. Reading a chat model outside its chat template reverses the sign of its gap with nothing at stake (-0.038 against +0.055 under the template on OLMo-3), a distortion present on two of three recipes. On both models that carry it, reasoning about the stakes before acting moves the choice back toward the model's own judgment, against a same-length non-moral task, with or without the pressure; on OLMo-3, naming the norm at stake does about a third of that. The gap is a measurable target for post-training recipes, not a fixed property of pretrained weights. 模型与技术突破 Principled Under Pressure: Post-Training Decides Whether LLMs Act on Their Own Moral Judgment 为什么值得关注？（模型能力变化与技术路线） 适合作为观察项：适合从模型能力变化、技术路线和产品化可能性角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv
发布时间：2026-10-06
关键词：cs.LG, cs.AI, cs.CL
57 观察 A Case Study in Assuring AI-Written Software Software-engineering agents can enable people without formal software training to build systems they could not otherwise implement and simultaneously can produce more code than even experts can meaningfully inspect. In both cases, exhaustive code review is not reliable as the sole basis for human control. We report a case study of a production healthcare platform built through coding agents and governed by an operator without formal software-engineering training. Over time, its workflow grew into a human-led meta-agent system where one agent wrote code, other agents supervised and reviewed it, and project rules carried lessons forward. The operator found that tests, monitors and reviewing agents used to supervise the system were fallible. Some monitors measured proxies rather than outcomes, some audits failed silently, missing checks disappeared from reported results and one automated repair caused operational disruption. In this case, human control depended on keeping the intended outcome, the evidence used to judge it, the agents' permissions and the final human decision were all tied to the same underlying objective. 模型与技术突破 A Case Study in Assuring AI-Written Software 为什么值得关注？（模型能力变化与技术路线） 适合作为观察项：适合从模型能力变化、技术路线和产品化可能性角度切入，来源：ArXiv。 来源：ArXiv
